new_task_1.title: Refresh stale system clock warning threshold
new_task_1.description: urllib3 2.2.0 refreshes the recent-date threshold used by connection code to detect materially stale local system clocks, changing RECENT_DATE from January 1, 2022 to June 1, 2023. This keeps the existing clock-skew diagnostic current for users whose incorrect system date could otherwise lead to confusing TLS verification failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure urllib3's stale-system-clock diagnostic uses a current recent-date threshold after upgrading to 2.2.0.

expectation.grounded: src/urllib3/connection.py should define RECENT_DATE as datetime.date(2023, 6, 1). Any connection logic that uses RECENT_DATE to decide whether the local system date is suspiciously old should use this updated threshold rather than the previous datetime.date(2022, 1, 1) value.
expectation.conceptual: Users with clocks set far in the past should continue receiving urllib3's existing warning before TLS failures become difficult to diagnose, and the cutoff should remain reasonably current for the 2.2.0 release.

constraints.grounded: Only the RECENT_DATE cutoff should change. The warning category, warning emission mechanism, TLS handshake behavior, certificate verification behavior, and connection APIs should remain otherwise unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This should be a diagnostic maintenance update, not a change to security policy or connection success criteria.

behavior: System-date freshness checks in connection handling use the updated threshold.
Local system dates before June 1, 2023 are treated as stale by the RECENT_DATE comparison, including dates that were after the old January 1, 2022 threshold.
Local system dates on or after June 1, 2023 are not considered stale solely because of the RECENT_DATE comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Given connection code evaluates the system date against RECENT_DATE, when the local date is May 31, 2023, then the stale-clock warning path should be selected.
Given connection code evaluates the system date against RECENT_DATE, when the local date is June 1, 2023 or later, then the stale-clock warning path should not be selected solely due to RECENT_DATE.

When urllib3 establishes HTTP or HTTPS connections, request behavior, TLS verification behavior, warning type, and public connection APIs should remain unchanged except for the updated stale-date cutoff.

new_task_2.title: Correct SOCKS dependency warning documentation link
new_task_2.description: urllib3 2.2.0 updates the user-facing DependencyWarning emitted when SOCKS support is imported without PySocks installed. The warning now points users to the SOCKS proxy guidance under advanced usage instead of the older contrib page anchor.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure the missing-PySocks diagnostic directs users to the current SOCKS proxy documentation.

expectation.grounded: In src/urllib3/contrib/socks.py, the ImportError fallback warning for missing PySocks should retain the existing SOCKS support and optional dependency wording while replacing https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contrib.html#socks-proxies with https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/advanced-usage.html#socks-proxies.
expectation.conceptual: Users who try to use SOCKS support without installing the optional dependency should receive the same dependency guidance, but the documentation link should take them to the current location.

constraints.grounded: Do not change PySocks import detection, the warning category, the optional dependency requirement, SOCKS proxy behavior when PySocks is installed, or exception behavior for unsupported SOCKS usage.
constraints.conceptual: This should improve guidance without changing dependency semantics or proxy transport behavior.

behavior: When urllib3.contrib.socks is imported without PySocks available, the emitted DependencyWarning includes the advanced-usage SOCKS proxy documentation URL.
The same warning no longer points to the older contrib.html SOCKS proxy anchor.
The warning continues to identify PySocks as the optional dependency required for SOCKS support.
When PySocks is installed, existing SOCKS support behavior remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given PySocks is unavailable, when urllib3.contrib.socks handles the import failure, then the DependencyWarning should contain https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/advanced-usage.html#socks-proxies.
Given PySocks is unavailable, when the warning is emitted, then it should not contain https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contrib.html#socks-proxies.
Given PySocks is unavailable, when the warning is emitted, then it should still be a DependencyWarning and should still state that PySocks is required for SOCKS support.
Given PySocks is installed, when urllib3.contrib.socks is imported and SOCKS proxies are used, then behavior should be unchanged by the documentation link update.
